hints: Focus on what cracking actually does, it splits one long alkane into a shorter alkane plus an alkene.
Check each formula with the alkane rule $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$ and the alkene rule $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}$, and remember carbons must still add to 17.
For each choice, work out what the partner fragment would have to be to balance C and H, and look for the one that leaves an impossible fragment.
walkthrough:
**Recall the cracking pattern**

Cracking breaks a long alkane into a shorter alkane and an alkene. No atoms are lost, so carbons and hydrogens must balance.

$$\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{36} \rightarrow \text{alkane (C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}) + \text{alkene (C}_m\text{H}_{2m})$$

**Test the small products**

A short alkane like $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$ leaves $\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{28}$, which is a fine alkene. A short alkene like $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$ leaves $\text{C}_{13}\text{H}_{28}$, which is a fine alkane. $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}$ leaves $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{20}$, also a fine pair.

$$\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{36} \rightarrow \text{C}_9\text{H}_{20} + \text{C}_8\text{H}_{16}$$

**Test the very long product**

If $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{34}$ (an alkene) formed, the other fragment must supply the rest of the atoms.

$$\text{C}_{17}\text{H}_{36} - \text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{34} = \text{CH}_2$$
That $\text{CH}_2$ fragment cannot exist on its own as methane, ethene or hydrogen. Cracking is meant to make usefully shorter chains, not to chop off one carbon, so this is the least likely.

options.A: C3H8 is an alkane (C3 fits CnH2n+2). It can form with C14H28 as the alkene partner, carbons 3+14=17 and hydrogens 8+28=36 balance perfectly, so it is a likely cracking product.
options.B: C4H8 is an alkene (C4 fits CnH2n). It can form with C13H28 as the alkane partner, carbons 4+13=17 and hydrogens 8+28=36 balance perfectly, so it is a likely cracking product.
options.C: C8H16 is an alkene (C8 fits CnH2n). It can form with C9H20 as the alkane partner, carbons 8+9=17 and hydrogens 16+20=36 balance perfectly, so it is a very typical cracking product.
options.D: C16H34 is an alkene with almost the same chain length as the starting material. Its partner would have to be CH2, which is not a stable product. Cracking aims to produce significantly shorter molecules, so this is least likely.
